questions.stem: In the number 75.64, which digit is in the hundredths place?

explanation: In 75.64, the 7 is in the tens place and the 5 is in the ones place.
After the decimal point, the 6 is in the tenths place and the 4 is in the hundredths place.
The digit in the hundredths place is 4, option (4).

questions.stem: Round 208 349 to the nearest thousand.

explanation: 208 349 lies between 208 000 and 209 000.
Look at the hundreds digit: it is 3, which is less than 5, so round down.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is correct?

explanation: Option (1): 6{1/2} = 6.5, not 6.2. Wrong.
Option (2): 6{7/10} = 6.7, and 6.09 is less than 6.7. Correct.
Option (3): 6.3 = 6.30, which is less than 6.33. Wrong.
Option (4): 6.050 is less than 6.505. Wrong.
The correct statement is option (2).

review.note: Misprint on the paper: it lists five lines, '(3) 6.3 > 6.33', '(4) 6.3 > 6.33' and '(4) 6.050 > 6.505'. The repeated line was dropped so that the four options are (1) to (4); the answer (2) is not affected.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is equal to 2 ÷ 7?

explanation: Dividing by 7 is the same as multiplying by {1/7}, so the answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Which one of the following shows that 40% of the figure is shaded?

images.alt: Four grids labelled (1) to (4). Each grid has 4 columns and 5 rows of equal squares, with some squares shaded. Figure (1) has 5 shaded squares, Figure (2) has 9, Figure (3) has 8 and Figure (4) has 10.

explanation: Each figure has 4 × 5 = 20 equal squares.
Count the shaded squares: Figure (1) has 5, Figure (2) has 9, Figure (3) has 8 and Figure (4) has 10.
Figure (3) has 8 shaded squares, so the answer is option (3).

questions.stem: The figures below show Square X of side 6 cm and Square Y of side 2 cm. What is the ratio of the area of Square X to the area of Square Y?

images.alt: Square X with side 6 cm and a smaller Square Y with side 2 cm.

explanation: Area of Square X = 6 × 6 = 36 cm².
Area of Square Y = 2 × 2 = 4 cm².
Area of X : area of Y = 36 : 4 = 9 : 1, option (4).

questions.stem: 25% of a number is 60. What is the number?

explanation: 25% is {1/4} of the number.
{1/4} of the number = 60, so the number = 4 × 60 = 240.
The number is 240, option (3).

questions.stem: The figure is made up of a semicircle and a quarter circle. O is the centre of the circle. AB = BC = 7 cm. Find the perimeter of the figure. (Take π = {22/7})

images.alt: A vertical straight line from A down through B to C. A quarter circle with centre C curves from A to the right end of a horizontal line through C. Below that horizontal line is a semicircle with centre O. Marks show AB, BC and the two radii on either side of O are equal.

explanation: The marks on the figure show that AB, BC and the radius of the semicircle are all 7 cm.
The quarter circle has centre C and radius AC = 7 + 7 = 14 cm. Its curved edge = {1/4} × 2 × {22/7} × 14 = 22 cm.
The semicircle has radius 7 cm. Its curved edge = {1/2} × 2 × {22/7} × 7 = 22 cm.
The straight edge AC = 14 cm.
Perimeter = 22 + 22 + 14 = 58 cm, option (2).

questions.stem: A rectangular container has a square base of side 4 cm and a height of 9 cm. What is the capacity of the container?

images.alt: A tall cuboid container with a square base of side 4 cm and height 9 cm.

explanation: Base area = 4 × 4 = 16 cm².
Capacity = base area × height = 16 × 9 = 144 cm³, option (3).

questions.stem: ABCD is a trapezium. Find ∠AFE.

images.alt: Trapezium ABCD with AD parallel to BC, AD on top and BC below. E is a point on AD and F is a point on AB. Line EF is drawn. Angle AEF is 28° and angle ABC is 123°. Angle AFE is marked.

explanation: AD is parallel to BC, so ∠BAD + ∠ABC = 180°.
In triangle AFE, ∠AFE = 180° − 57° − 28° = 95°, option (2).

questions.stem: Which of the following fractions is closest to {1/2}?

explanation: Find how much more than {1/2} each fraction is.
The smallest difference is {1/14}, so {4/7} is closest to {1/2}, option (2).

questions.stem: Find the area of triangle PQR.

images.alt: A 6 by 6 grid of 1 cm squares. P is on the top edge, 4 squares from the left. Q is on the left edge, 1 square up from the bottom. R is at the bottom right corner. Triangle PQR is drawn.

explanation: The grid is a 6 cm by 6 cm square with area 6 × 6 = 36 cm². P is on the top side, 4 cm from the left. Q is on the left side, 1 cm from the bottom. R is the bottom right corner.
Subtract the three right-angled triangles around triangle PQR.
Top left triangle: {1/2} × 4 × 5 = 10 cm².
Right triangle: {1/2} × 2 × 6 = 6 cm².
Bottom triangle: {1/2} × 6 × 1 = 3 cm².
Area of triangle PQR = 36 − 10 − 6 − 3 = 17 cm², option (2).

questions.stem: Jacy used {2/5} of a packet of flour to bake cookies. Then she used 210 g of flour to bake tarts. In the end, she had 150 g of flour left. What was the total mass of flour Jacy used to bake cookies and tarts?

explanation: After the cookies, 1 − {2/5} = {3/5} of the packet was left.
{3/5} of the packet = 210 + 150 = 360 g.
{1/5} of the packet = 360 ÷ 3 = 120 g, so the whole packet = 5 × 120 = 600 g.
Flour used = 600 − 150 = 450 g, option (3).

questions.stem:
The pie charts show the number of each type of fruits in two baskets, A and B. The total number of fruits in Basket A is twice the total number of fruits in Basket B.
[[img1]]
Which one of the following statements is not correct?

images.alt: Two pie charts. Basket A: Orange 65%, Peach (marked with a right angle at the centre) and Kiwi. Basket B: Kiwi 35%, Orange 45% and Peach.

options: {1/10} of the fruits in Basket A are kiwis.
There are more peaches in Basket A than in Basket B.
Basket A contains three times as many oranges as Basket B.
The ratio of the number of oranges to the number of kiwis in Basket B is 9 : 7.

explanation: Basket A: the peach part has a right angle, so peaches are 25%. Kiwis = 100% − 65% − 25% = 10%.
Basket B: peaches = 100% − 35% − 45% = 20%.
Suppose Basket B has 100 fruits. Then Basket A has 200 fruits.
Basket A: 130 oranges, 50 peaches, 20 kiwis. Basket B: 45 oranges, 20 peaches, 35 kiwis.
(1) 20 out of 200 = {1/10}. Correct. (2) 50 peaches is more than 20 peaches. Correct. (4) 45 : 35 = 9 : 7. Correct.
(3) 3 × 45 = 135, but Basket A has 130 oranges. Not correct.
The statement that is not correct is option (3).

questions.stem:
The table shows the airmail rates to two countries.
[[table1]]
Mr Fang sent a parcel weighing 4.5 kg to Japan and a parcel weighing 8.1 kg to Australia. How much did he pay altogether?

rows: Every additional 1 kg or part thereof

explanation: Japan: 4.5 kg is not more than 5 kg, so the parcel costs $30.
Australia: the first 5 kg costs $40. Extra mass = 8.1 − 5 = 3.1 kg.
3.1 kg counts as 4 additional kilograms because part of a kilogram is charged as a full one: 4 × $7 = $28.
Australia parcel = $40 + $28 = $68.

questions.stem: 6 identical pails of water can fill {1/3} of a tank. Ryden needs another 3 such pails and 20 identical jugs of water to fill the tank completely. Each jug can hold 0.9 ℓ of water. Find the capacity of the tank.

explanation: 6 pails fill {1/3} of the tank, so 3 pails fill {1/6} of the tank.
6 pails and 3 pails together fill {1/3} + {1/6} = {1/2} of the tank.
The 20 jugs fill the other {1/2} of the tank: 20 × 0.9 = 18 ℓ.
Capacity of the tank = 2 × 18 = 36 ℓ, option (3).

questions.stem:
A roll of sticker has pictures that follow a repeated pattern as shown.
Mrs Han cut out a length of ribbon containing 41 ♡ (hearts).
What was the greatest possible number of ✹ (suns) that were in the length of stickers Mrs Han cut out?

images.alt: A strip of stickers starting from the left end of the roll: sun, heart, lightning, sun, moon, sun, heart, lightning, sun, moon, sun, heart, lightning, and then the strip continues.

explanation: The pattern repeats every 5 stickers: sun, heart, lightning, sun, moon. Each group has 1 heart and 2 suns.
Mrs Han cuts from the start of the roll. To get 41 hearts she needs 41 complete groups: 41 × 2 = 82 suns.
She can cut a little further without reaching another heart. The 42nd group starts with a sun, and the sticker after it is a heart, so she can take 1 more sun.
Greatest number of suns = 82 + 1 = 83, option (3).

review.solvedAnswer: 3 (cut from the start of the roll) or 4 (cut from anywhere)
review.note: The answer depends on where the length is cut. If it is cut from the start of the roll, as the picture suggests (the roll begins with a sun), the most is 41 × 2 + 1 = 83, which is the key's answer (3). If the length may be cut from the middle of the roll, it can also start just after a heart and take 2 more suns in front (lightning, sun, moon, sun), giving 2 + 80 + 2 = 84, option (4). The key's answer is stored. The paper also says 'length of ribbon' in one line and 'length of stickers' in the next; transcribed as printed. The heart and sun pictures in the text were replaced by symbols with the words in brackets.

questions.stem:
Figure 1 shows a right-angled triangle with a perimeter of 40 cm. Figure 2 is made up of two such triangles. The perimeter of figure 2 is 64 cm. The length of AC is 17 cm.
[[img1]]
Find the area of one right-angled triangle.

images.alt: Figure 1: right-angled triangle ABC with the right angle at B and longest side AC. Figure 2: two such triangles joined. The shortest side of the left triangle lies along part of the longest side of the right triangle, which is drawn vertically.

explanation: Two separate triangles have a total perimeter of 40 + 40 = 80 cm.
In Figure 2 the shortest side BC of one triangle lies along the longest side of the other, so a length equal to BC is hidden on each triangle.
2 × BC = 80 − 64 = 16 cm, so BC = 8 cm.
The right angle is at B, so area = {1/2} × AB × BC = {1/2} × 15 × 8 = 60 cm², option (1).

review.note: The paper prints 'The length of AC is AC is 17 cm.'; the repeated words were removed.

questions.stem:
The solid is made up of 14 cubes.
[[img1]]

images.alt: A solid of 1 cm cubes stacked like steps in a corner: 3 by 3 cubes on the bottom layer, 2 by 2 cubes on the middle layer and 1 cube on top, all against the back left corner. Arrows show the top view from above, the front view from the front and the side view from the right.
A glass box 10 cm long, 5 cm wide and 6 cm high with the solid of 14 cubes sitting in one corner.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Draw the side view on the grid. (Draw it on your canvas, then check.)

answer.value: A staircase shape 3 squares wide: the left column is 1 square tall, the middle column is 2 squares tall and the right column is 3 squares tall, all standing on the same base line.

explanation: The solid has 3 layers: 9 cubes (3 by 3) at the bottom, 4 cubes (2 by 2) in the middle and 1 cube on top, all pushed into the back left corner. 9 + 4 + 1 = 14.
From the side, you see 3 columns. The row nearest the front is 1 cube tall, the middle row is 2 cubes tall and the back row is 3 cubes tall.
Looking from the side shown, the front of the solid is on your left. So draw columns of 1, 2 and 3 squares from left to right, 6 squares in all.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
The 14 cubes are then placed in a glass box as shown. How many more such cubes are needed to fill the box completely?
[[img2]]
explanation: The box is 10 cm by 5 cm by 6 cm, and each cube has a side of 1 cm.
Number of cubes that fill the box = 10 × 5 × 6 = 300.
Number of cubes still needed = 300 − 14 = 286.

review.keyAnswer: a) staircase of 1, 2 and 3 squares from left to right  b) 286

questions.stem: In the figure, JKLM is a rectangle. JPL and MPN are straight lines. ∠KJL = 58° and ∠KNM = 137°. Find ∠JPM.

images.alt: Rectangle JKLM with J top left, M top right, K bottom left and L bottom right. Diagonal JL is drawn. N is on side KL and line MN crosses JL at P. Angle KJL is 58° and angle KNM is 137°.

explanation: In triangle JKL, ∠JKL = 90°, so ∠JLK = 180° − 90° − 58° = 32°.
KNL is a straight line, so ∠PNL = 180° − 137° = 43°.
In triangle PNL, ∠NPL = 180° − 32° − 43° = 105°.
∠JPM and ∠NPL are vertically opposite angles, so ∠JPM = 105°.

questions.stem:
The table shows the prices of buffet lunch at Sunny Spoon Restaurant.
[[table1]]

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: 3 adults had lunch. How much money did they pay altogether?
explanation: Each adult pays $54.
3 adults pay 3 × $54 = $162.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What was the least amount of money that 5 adults and 4 children had to pay for the buffet lunch?
explanation: Without the package, 2 adults and 2 children pay 2 × $54 + 2 × $42 = $192. The Family Package costs $170, so it is cheaper.
5 adults and 4 children can use 2 Family Packages (4 adults and 4 children): 2 × $170 = $340.
The 1 adult left pays $54.
Least amount = $340 + $54 = $394.

questions.stem:
The table shows the prices of different types of pizzas sold at The Happy Crust.
[[table1]]

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Gillian bought 2 pepperoni and 3 hawaiian pizzas. How much money did she spend altogether? Give your answer in terms of k.
explanation: 2 pepperoni pizzas cost 2 × $(k + 3) = $(2k + 6).
3 hawaiian pizzas cost 3 × $k = $3k.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Given k = 12, what was the total amount of money Gillian spent on the 2 pepperoni and 3 hawaiian pizzas?
explanation: Put k = 12 into 5k + 6.
Gillian spent $66.

questions.stem:
The figure shows the net of a cuboid.
[[img1]]
Find the volume of the cuboid.

images.alt: Net of a cuboid made of three rows of equal height. Top row: one long rectangle. Middle row: a long rectangle, a small square and another long rectangle. Bottom row: a small square followed by a long rectangle. The three rows are 30 cm high in total. The small square in the bottom row is 10 cm wide and the middle row is 110 cm long.

explanation: The net has 3 rows of the same height, and the total height is 30 cm, so each row is 30 ÷ 3 = 10 cm high.
The small face on the left is 10 cm wide and 10 cm high, so the two end faces are squares of side 10 cm.
The 110 cm length is made up of a long face, a 10 cm square face and another long face.
Length of each long face = (110 − 10) ÷ 2 = 50 cm.
The cuboid is 50 cm by 10 cm by 10 cm. Volume = 50 × 10 × 10 = 5000 cm³.

questions.stem: In the figure, PQR and STU are equilateral triangles. ∠RXT = 83°.

images.alt: Equilateral triangle PQR with P bottom left, Q bottom right and R on top. S is a point on PQ near P. Equilateral triangle STU has U at the top left and T at the top right. Line US crosses PR at W. Line ST crosses RQ at X. Angle RXT is 83° and angle TSQ is 37°.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find ∠PWS.
explanation: Each angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°, so ∠UST = 60° and ∠RPQ = 60°.
PSQ is a straight line, so ∠WSP = 180° − 60° − 37° = 83°.
In triangle PWS, ∠PWS = 180° − 60° − 83° = 37°.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
Each of the statements below is either true, false or not possible to tell from the information given.
(i) Triangle TXQ is a right-angled triangle.
(ii) Triangle PWS is an isosceles triangle.
(Type your answer for (i), then (ii), separated by a comma. Use true, false or not possible to tell.)
explanation: (i) RXQ is a straight line, so ∠TXQ = 180° − 83° = 97°. The other two angles of triangle TXQ add up to 180° − 97° = 83°, so neither of them can be 90°. The triangle has no right angle: False.
(ii) The angles of triangle PWS are 60°, 83° and 37°. No two angles are equal, so it is not isosceles: False.
The answers are False and False.

questions.stem:
At a fun fair, 60 people participated in a game where they had to burst balloons within a given time. The table shows the number of balloons burst by each participant.
[[table1]]
What was the total number of balloons burst?

explanation: Multiply each number of balloons by the number of participants who burst that many.
Total = 0 + 19 + 26 + 24 + 24 = 93 balloons.

The pie chart and bar graph show the favourite ice cream flavour of a group of students.
[[img1]]
[[img2]]

images.alt: Pie chart with four parts: Chocolate {3/8}, Strawberry, Hazelnut {1/4} (marked with a right angle at the centre) and Vanilla.
Bar graph of number of students, scale 0 to 80 in steps of 10 with a line every 5. Strawberry 50, Chocolate (no bar drawn), Vanilla 25, Hazelnut 50.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Draw the bar graph that shows the number of students who chose chocolate as their favourite ice cream flavour. (Draw it on your canvas, then check.)

answer.value: A bar for Chocolate that reaches 75, halfway between 70 and 80.

explanation: Hazelnut is {1/4} of the students, and the bar graph shows 50 students chose hazelnut.
Total number of students = 4 × 50 = 200.
Chocolate = {3/8} × 200 = 75 students.
Draw the Chocolate bar up to 75, halfway between the 70 and 80 lines.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What percentage of the students chose vanilla as their favourite ice cream flavour?
explanation: The bar graph shows 25 students chose vanilla, and there are 200 students altogether.

questions.stem:
Figure PSRTQ has an area of 140 cm². PQ is a straight line. Triangle PQT and triangle PQS are identical.
[[img1]]
What is the area of triangle PRQ?

images.alt: Base PQ is 7 cm long. Triangle PQS has S high up on the left, 24 cm above the level of PQ (shown by a dotted height with a right angle). Triangle PQT has T high up on the right. Lines QS and PT cross at R above PQ.

explanation: Triangle PQS has base PQ = 7 cm and height 24 cm. Area = {1/2} × 7 × 24 = 84 cm².
Triangle PQT is identical, so its area is also 84 cm².
The two triangles overlap at triangle PRQ. Adding them counts triangle PRQ twice: 84 + 84 = 168 cm².
Area of triangle PRQ = 168 − 140 = 28 cm².

questions.stem: At Happy Plates Shop, Aubrey and Linsy each spent $72 on some similar plates. As a member of Happy Plates Shop, Linsy was given a 25% discount. In the end, Linsy bought 2 more plates than Aubrey.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many plates did Linsy buy?
explanation: With a 25% discount, Linsy paid 75% = {3/4} of the usual price for each plate.
For every 4 units of money Aubrey paid for a plate, Linsy paid 3 units. With the same $72, Aubrey could buy 3 plates for every 4 plates Linsy bought.
Linsy : Aubrey = 4 : 3. The difference is 1 unit = 2 plates.
Linsy bought 4 × 2 = 8 plates.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What was the cost of one plate before the discount?
explanation: Aubrey bought 3 × 2 = 6 plates at the usual price for $72.
Cost of one plate before the discount = $72 ÷ 6 = $12.

questions.stem:
At a food fair, for every purchase of 5 drumsticks, a discount of $1 was given.
[[img1]]
Brayden gave the cashier $60 and he received a change of $4. How many drumsticks did he buy?

images.alt: A sign: Drumstick Sale! $2 for 1 drumstick. Buy 5 drumsticks, get a $1 discount. A bucket of drumsticks is pictured.

explanation: Brayden paid $60 − $4 = $56.
A group of 5 drumsticks costs 5 × $2 − $1 = $9.
$56 ÷ $9 = 6 groups with $2 left over. 6 groups = 6 × 5 = 30 drumsticks.
The $2 left over buys 1 more drumstick.
Brayden bought 30 + 1 = 31 drumsticks.

questions.stem: Michelle bought some green and red apples. {1/4} of the green apples and {1/7} of the red apples were large. She bought 36 large apples altogether and {4/9} of the large apples were green. What fraction of the apples were large red apples?

explanation: Large green apples = {4/9} × 36 = 16. Large red apples = 36 − 16 = 20.
{1/4} of the green apples = 16, so there were 4 × 16 = 64 green apples.
{1/7} of the red apples = 20, so there were 7 × 20 = 140 red apples.
Total number of apples = 64 + 140 = 204.
Fraction that were large red apples = {20/204} = {5/51}.

questions.stem: A ribbon measuring 1{4/5} m was cut into 2 pieces. The shorter piece was 37 cm long. What was the difference in length between the two pieces of ribbon?

explanation: Longer piece = 180 − 37 = 143 cm.
Difference = 143 − 37 = 106 cm.

questions.stem:
The figure is made up of equilateral triangles of different sizes. The area of the shaded triangle is 8 cm².
[[img1]]
What is the total area of the unshaded parts?

images.alt: Two large equilateral triangles of the same size joined along a side to form a parallelogram: the left one points down and the right one points up. Inside the right triangle, the midpoints of its sides are joined to form a smaller triangle pointing down. Inside that triangle, the midpoints are joined again to form the smallest triangle, which is shaded.

explanation: Joining the midpoints of the sides of an equilateral triangle cuts it into 4 identical smaller triangles.
The shaded triangle is 1 of the 4 small triangles inside the middle triangle, so the middle triangle = 4 × 8 = 32 cm².
The middle triangle is 1 of the 4 triangles inside the big triangle on the right, so that big triangle = 4 × 32 = 128 cm².
The marks show that the triangle on the left has the same side length as the big triangle on the right, so its area is also 128 cm².
Whole figure = 128 + 128 = 256 cm².
Unshaded area = 256 − 8 = 248 cm².

questions.stem:
The table shows the five activities that a group of children attended during the June holidays. Each child attended only one activity.
[[table1]]

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The average number of children who attended each activity was 161. How many children took part in Dance?
explanation: Total number of children = 5 × 161 = 805.
Children in the other four activities = 84 + 153 + 108 + 216 = 561.
Dance = 805 − 561 = 244 children.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Each child paid $80 to take part in Hiking. The total amount of money collected for Hiking was $2424 more than the total amount collected for Art and Craft. How much did each child pay for Art and Craft?
explanation: Money collected for Hiking = 108 × $80 = $8640.
Money collected for Art and Craft = $8640 − $2424 = $6216.
Each child paid $6216 ÷ 84 = $74 for Art and Craft.

questions.stem: Derrick filled a tank with water using two taps. He turned on Tap A first. 10 minutes later, he turned on Tap B. Both taps were turned off at the same time when the tank was completely filled without overflowing.

images.alt: Line graph of amount of water in litres (0 to 80) against time in minutes (0 to 40). The line rises from 0 litres at 0 minutes to 10 litres at 10 minutes, passes through 40 litres at 20 minutes, reaches 70 litres at 30 minutes and then stays level at 70 litres until 40 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: 10 minutes after Tap A was turned on, what fraction of the tank was filled? Leave your answer in the simplest form.
explanation: From the graph, the tank had 10 litres of water after 10 minutes.
The graph stops rising at 70 litres, so the full tank holds 70 litres.
Fraction filled = {10/70} = {1/7}.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: In one minute, how many litres of water flowed into the tank from both Tap A and Tap B?
explanation: Both taps were on from 10 minutes to 30 minutes, which is 20 minutes.
In that time the water rose from 10 litres to 70 litres: 70 − 10 = 60 litres.
In one minute, 60 ÷ 20 = 3 litres flowed in from both taps.

questions.stem:
ABCD is a square and CD = CF. AC and BF are straight lines.
[[img1]]
Find ∠BFC.

images.alt: Square ABCD with A top left, D top right, B bottom left and C bottom right. Diagonal AC is drawn. F is a point inside the square near the top side, joined to B, C and D. BF crosses AC at E. The angle between CA and CF at C is 19°. Angles BFC and FDC are marked.

explanation: AC is a diagonal of the square, so ∠ACB = 45°.
CB = CD because ABCD is a square, and CD = CF, so CB = CF. Triangle BCF is isosceles.

questions.stem: Jar A and Jar B contained 946 marbles altogether. Jar A contained more marbles than Jar B. When another 280 marbles were put into Jar B, Jar A had 120 more marbles than Jar B. How many marbles did Jar B contain at first?

explanation: After 280 marbles were added to Jar B, Jar A still had 120 more. So at first Jar A had 280 + 120 = 400 more marbles than Jar B.
Take away the extra 400 marbles: 946 − 400 = 546. This is 2 times the number in Jar B.
Jar B at first = 546 ÷ 2 = 273 marbles.

questions.stem: An aquarium has three types of fish. There are 14n goldfish. There are 8n fewer guppies than goldfish. There are 4 more angelfish than guppies.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the number of angelfish in terms of n.
explanation: Number of guppies = 14n − 8n = 6n.
Number of angelfish = 6n + 4.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: There are 76 angelfish. Find the value of n.

questions.stem: The figure shows a triangle ADF, a parallelogram GCDE and an isosceles triangle BCG with GB = GC.

images.alt: (The picture is printed sideways.) Triangle ADF with base AD and top corner F. B and C are points on AD, in the order A, B, C, D. G is on side AF and E is on side FD. GCDE is a parallelogram with GE parallel to CD and GC parallel to ED. G is also joined to B. Angle FGE is 58° and angle AGB is 21°. Angles GAB and BGC are marked.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find ∠BGC.
explanation: GE is parallel to CD because GCDE is a parallelogram, so ∠GAB = ∠FGE = 58° (corresponding angles).
∠GBC is an exterior angle of triangle ABG: ∠GBC = 58° + 21° = 79°.
GB = GC, so ∠GCB = ∠GBC = 79°.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find ∠EFG.
explanation: GC is parallel to ED, so ∠EDC = ∠GCB = 79° (corresponding angles).
In triangle ADF, ∠FAD = 58° and ∠ADF = 79°.

review.note: This page is printed sideways in the PDF, so the cropped figure appears rotated a quarter turn. The format has no way to rotate a crop.

questions.stem:
The bar graph shows the number of buns Mr Tong baked to sell.
[[img1]]
The table shows the percentage of each type of buns that were not sold.
[[table1]]

images.alt: Bar graph of number of buns baked, scale 0 to 450 in steps of 50 with a line every 10. Hotdog 420, Cheese 250, Tuna 300, Curry 380.

rows: Percentage of each type of buns not sold

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the ratio of the number of tuna buns baked to the number of tuna buns sold. Give your answer in the simplest form.
explanation: 20% of the tuna buns were not sold, so 100% − 20% = 80% were sold.
Check with the graph: 300 tuna buns were baked and 80% × 300 = 240 were sold. 300 : 240 = 5 : 4.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Mr Tong collected $387 from selling cheese buns. How much did one cheese bun cost?
explanation: From the graph, 250 cheese buns were baked.
14% were not sold, so 100% − 14% = 86% were sold.
Cheese buns sold = {86/100} × 250 = 215.
Cost of one cheese bun = $387 ÷ 215 = $1.80.

questions.stem: A bottle contains 1792 cm³ of water when placed upright and the height of the water level is 16 cm. When the same bottle is turned upside down, there is a 5 cm gap between the base and the water level.

images.alt: Left: a bottle shaped like a cuboid with a narrow neck on top, standing upright with water up to a height of 16 cm. Right: the same bottle turned upside down, with the water filling the neck and most of the body and a 5 cm empty gap between the water level and the base, which is now on top.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the base area of the bottle?
explanation: When the bottle is upright, the water fills a cuboid 16 cm high.
Base area = 1792 ÷ 16 = 112 cm².

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What is the capacity of the bottle?
explanation: When the bottle is upside down, the empty space is a cuboid with the same base and a height of 5 cm.
Empty space = 112 × 5 = 560 cm³.
Capacity = water + empty space = 1792 + 560 = 2352 cm³ = 2352 ml.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Half of the water in the bottle is poured into some empty containers. All the containers are filled to the brim. Each container has a capacity of 128 cm³. How many such containers are completely filled with water?
explanation: Half of the water = 1792 ÷ 2 = 896 cm³.
7 containers are completely filled.

questions.stem: Amira, Bianca and Cecilia sold some bracelets. Each bracelet cost $7.80. Amira sold {1/5} of the bracelets. Bianca and Cecilia sold the rest of the bracelets in the ratio 3 : 2. Cecilia sold 102 more bracelets than Amira.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many bracelets did the three of them sell altogether?
explanation: Bianca and Cecilia sold 1 − {1/5} = {4/5} of the bracelets, shared in the ratio 3 : 2, which is 5 parts.
To make the parts easy to share, cut the total into 25 units. Amira sold 5 units, and the other two sold 20 units.
Bianca sold {3/5} × 20 = 12 units and Cecilia sold {2/5} × 20 = 8 units.
Cecilia − Amira = 8 − 5 = 3 units = 102 bracelets, so 1 unit = 102 ÷ 3 = 34.
Total = 25 × 34 = 850 bracelets.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How much more money did Bianca collect than Amira?
explanation: Bianca sold 12 − 5 = 7 units more than Amira: 7 × 34 = 238 bracelets.
Bianca collected $1856.40 more than Amira.

The figure is made up of rows of identical triangles.
[[img1]]
Study the pattern carefully.

images.alt: A large triangle made of 4 rows of small identical triangles. Row 1 at the top has 1 triangle, Row 2 has 3, Row 3 has 5 and Row 4 at the bottom has 7. The shading does not show in the scan; going by the table, the triangles pointing up are the shaded ones and the triangles pointing down are the unshaded ones.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
The table shows the number of triangles used for each row. Fill in the table for Row 5.
[[table1]]
(Type the two missing numbers separated by a comma: the number of unshaded triangles, then the total number of triangles.)
explanation: The number of unshaded triangles is 1 less than the row number: 5 − 1 = 4.
Total number of triangles in Row 5 = 5 + 4 = 9. (The totals go up by 2 each row: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.)
The missing numbers are 4 and 9.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How many unshaded triangles are there in Row 200?
explanation: The number of unshaded triangles is always 1 less than the row number.
Row 200 has 200 − 1 = 199 unshaded triangles.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A row has a total number of 327 triangles. What is the row number?
explanation: Total = shaded + unshaded = row number + (row number − 1). So the total is 1 less than 2 times the row number.
2 × row number = 327 + 1 = 328.
Row number = 328 ÷ 2 = 164.

questions.stem: Vivian bought some beads. She sewed {3/7} of the beads onto 2 dresses and 7 skirts. She then had 960 beads left.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What was the total number of beads Vivian sewed onto the 2 dresses and 7 skirts?
explanation: Beads left = 1 − {3/7} = {4/7} of the beads = 960.
Beads sewn = {3/7} of the beads = 3 × 240 = 720.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: On each dress, Vivian sewed {1/4} as many beads as she sewed onto each skirt. How many beads did she sew onto each skirt?
explanation: Let the beads on each dress be 1 unit. Then each skirt has 4 units.
2 dresses = 2 × 1 = 2 units. 7 skirts = 7 × 4 = 28 units.
Altogether 2 + 28 = 30 units = 720 beads, so 1 unit = 720 ÷ 30 = 24.
Each skirt has 4 × 24 = 96 beads.

review.note: The mark bracket for part (b) is missing from the scan. It is taken as 3 marks so that Questions 6 to 15 add up to the 40 marks printed in the section header.

questions.stem:
The figure shows a square, ABCD, in a circle. AC and BD are the diameters of the circle. The diameter of the circle is 56 cm.
[[img1]]

images.alt: A circle with square ABCD inside it, drawn as a diamond with B on top, C on the right, D at the bottom and A on the left. The diagonals AC and BD are drawn. Four curved lines, each a quarter circle, join A to B, B to C, C to D and D to A, bending in towards the centre to make a four-pointed star. The four parts between the sides of the square and the curved lines are shaded.
Figure 1: the square ABCD cut out, drawn as a diamond with B on top, C right, D bottom and A left, with the four-pointed star inside it.

Figure 2: a rectangular cardboard, 390 cm wide (and 6.4 m long). Diamonds are pasted in the top left corner, touching corner to corner: two side by side along the top edge and one below the first, with dots showing the pattern continues across and down.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the total area of the shaded parts. (Take π = {22/7})
explanation: The radius of the circle is 56 ÷ 2 = 28 cm. AC and BD cut the square into 4 identical right-angled triangles with two sides of 28 cm.

Each curved line is a quarter circle of radius 28 cm that fits in a 28 cm by 28 cm square with the side of square ABCD as its diagonal. Each shaded part is this quarter circle minus a right-angled triangle.
Quarter circle = {1/4} × {22/7} × 28 × 28 = 616 cm².
One shaded part = 616 − 392 = 224 cm².
Total shaded area = 4 × 224 = 896 cm².

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
Square ABCD was cut out from the circle as shown in Figure 1. A number of such squares were pasted on a rectangular cardboard, 6.4 m long and 390 cm wide, following the pattern as shown. Figure 2 shows part of the arrangement. What is the greatest number of such squares that can be pasted on the cardboard?
[[img2]]
[[img3]]
explanation: Each square is pasted like a diamond, so it takes up 56 cm across and 56 cm down (the lengths of its diagonals AC and BD).
6.4 m = 640 cm. Along the length: 640 ÷ 56 = 11 remainder 24, so 11 squares fit.
Along the width: 390 ÷ 56 = 6 remainder 54, so 6 squares fit.
Greatest number of squares = 11 × 6 = 66.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The greatest number of squares are pasted on the cardboard without overlapping. What is the area of the cardboard that is not covered by the squares?
explanation: Area of the cardboard = 640 × 390 = 249 600 cm².
Area of one square = {1/2} × 56 × 56 = 1568 cm² (half the product of its diagonals, or 4 triangles of 392 cm²).
Area of 66 squares = 66 × 1568 = 103 488 cm².
Area not covered = 249 600 − 103 488 = 146 112 cm².

review.note: Resolved on review (answer differs from or goes beyond the printed key; the stored answer was re-checked): Parts (a) and (b) match the key. For part (c) the key prints 114112, but 640 × 390 − 66 × 1568 = 249 600 − 103 488 = 146 112. The key's figure looks like a typing slip for 146112 (no reasonable reading of the question gives 114112), so 146112 is stored. Someone has also handwritten '= 640 cm' beside the 6.4 m label on the scan; the Figure 2 crop stops just above that label line, and the length is given in the question text.

questions.stem:
Huahua has a triangular piece of paper ACE with ∠ACE = 82°. She then folded along the lines BD and FG as shown in the figure.
[[img1]]

images.alt: Before folding: triangle ACE with A top left, E top right and C at the bottom, angle ACE = 82°. B is on AC, D is on CE, F is on AE and G is on CE near E. Dotted fold lines BD and FG are shown with arrows. After folding: corner C is folded up over line BD so that it lies above line AF, with angle BCD = 82°. Corner E is folded down over line FG. The angle at F between FA and the folded edge FE is 120°. The angle at D between DC and the edge DG is 78°. Arrows show that the folded edge FE is parallel to DC. Angles FAB, ABD, CBD and BDC are marked.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find ∠CBD.
explanation: Before folding, CDE is a straight line. Folding along BD moves the corner C, and the folded ∠BDC is equal to the ∠BDC before folding.
At D, the two equal angles and the 78° angle make a straight line: 2 × ∠BDC + 78° = 180°.
In triangle BCD, ∠CBD = 180° − 82° − 51° = 47°.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find ∠FAB.
explanation: After folding, the edge FE crosses the edge DG. Call the crossing point X.
AF was part of the straight line AFE, so the angle between the folded edge FE and the old position of FE is 180° − 120° = 60°.
The arrows show that the folded edge FE is parallel to DC. So ∠FXG = 78° (corresponding angles).
Unfold the flap. In the triangle made by F, X and the old position of E, the angle at F is 60° and the angle at X is 78°, so the angle at E is 180° − 60° − 78° = 42°. This is ∠AEC of the paper.
In triangle ACE, ∠FAB = 180° − 82° − 42° = 56°.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt:
Circle the words that describe ABCD in the statement:
AB ( is / is not ) parallel to CD because ∠ABD and ∠BDC ( add / do not add ) up to 180°.
(Type the two choices separated by a comma, for example: is, add.)

accept: is not and do not add

explanation: ABC was a straight line before folding, so ∠ABD = 180° − 47° = 133°.
∠ABD + ∠BDC = 133° + 51° = 184°, which is not 180°.
If AB were parallel to CD, these two angles would add up to 180°. They do not, so AB is not parallel to CD.

review.keyAnswer: a) 47  b) 56  c) is not; do not add
review.solvedAnswer: a) 47  b) 56  c) is not, do not add
